# Vendored browser files: sources and provenance

This directory holds every third-party JavaScript, CSS, font, and binary-data
file the Studio web UI loads directly in the browser. Nothing here is fetched
from a CDN at runtime. Each file below is either a byte-for-byte frozen copy
of an npm package file, a file generated from `node_modules` by a build
script, or a hand-patched copy (see `patches/`).

Versions pinned in `package.json`: `three@0.185.0`, `@picocss/pico@2.1.1`,
`lucide-static@1.47.0` (dev dependency), `@fontsource/ibm-plex-sans@5.3.0`
(dev dependency), `jsep@1.4.0`.

@fontsource/ibm-plex-sans@5.3.0, jsep@1.4.0 — the exact versions pinned in
`package.json`). Only `three.core.js` differs from its npm build; see
`patches/three.core.js.patch`. All license files were also byte-diffed
against their `node_modules` originals and are unmodified.

## The `three.core.js` patch

`patches/three.core.js.patch` is a unified diff (`node_modules` version →
vendored version) touching one line inside `ShapePath.prototype.toShapes()`,
the routine that resolves nested/overlapping SVG (and font-glyph) subpaths
into filled shapes with holes. For each candidate ancestor subpath, the
upstream code decides "is `entry` nested inside `candidate`?" by checking
only whether `candidate`'s bounding box contains `entry`'s single interior
point, then running the expensive point-in-polygon test. The vendored copy
tightens that pre-check to require `candidate`'s bounding box to fully
contain `entry`'s entire bounding box before running the point-in-polygon
test.

Why this might have been changed: a bounding box can contain a single
interior point without truly enclosing the other shape (e.g. two sibling
subpaths whose boxes only overlap in one corner, or a hole that pokes outside
its nominal container along one axis) — the interior-point check alone can
misclassify such a sibling as a container. Requiring full bounding-box
containment first is a cheap, strictly-more-conservative filter that rules
those false positives out before falling back on the exact point-in-polygon
test, which should make nested-hole resolution more correct for glyphs/paths
whose subpaths are not cleanly nested along both axes. This reading is
inferred from the code and the geometry of `Box2`/`containsBox`/
`containsPoint`; no upstream three.js issue or PR discussion for this
specific line was found in this repo, so the exact triggering case cannot be
confirmed from the diff alone.

## How to refresh

Running `npm run build:app` (which runs `build:ui` first) regenerates:

- `ui/pico.css`, `ui/icons.js`, `ui/plex-{400,500,600}.woff2`,
  `ui/PICO-LICENSE`, `ui/LUCIDE-LICENSE`, `ui/FONT-LICENSE`
  (via `scripts/build_ui_assets.mjs`)
- `addons/loaders/DRACOLoader.js`, `addons/loaders/KTX2Loader.js`,
  `addons/utils/WorkerPool.js`, `addons/math/ColorSpaces.js`,
  `addons/libs/ktx-parse.module.js`, `addons/libs/zstddec.module.js`,
  `addons/libs/meshopt_decoder.module.js`, `gltf-codec-data.js`
  (via `scripts/build_gltf_codecs.mjs`)

Everything else in this directory must be copied by hand when the pinned
package version changes:

- `three.core.js`, `three.module.js` — copy from
  `node_modules/three/build/`. **`three.core.js` carries a hand patch**
  (see above); after copying a new `three.core.js`, re-apply
  `patches/three.core.js.patch` with `patch -p0 --fuzz=0 <
  studio/web/vendor/patches/three.core.js.patch` (adjust the line offsets by
  hand if the patch no longer applies cleanly against the new upstream file),
  then re-diff against the fresh npm copy to regenerate the `.patch` file so
  it always reflects the current delta.
- `addons/controls/OrbitControls.js`, `addons/controls/TransformControls.js`,
  `addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js`, `addons/loaders/STLLoader.js`,
  `addons/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js`, `addons/utils/SkeletonUtils.js` —
  copy from `node_modules/three/examples/jsm/...`.
- `jsep.js` — copy from `node_modules/jsep/dist/jsep.js`.
- `motionforge/*.js` — hand-ported from the author-owned MotionForge project;
  follow the patch list and re-verify the SHA-256 pairs recorded in
  `motionforge/SOURCES.json` (owned by another agent — do not edit here).
- `*-LICENSE*` files without a generating script (`THREE-LICENSE.txt`,
  `DRACO-LICENSE.txt`, `BASIS-LICENSE.txt`, `MESHOPT-LICENSE.txt`,
  `KTX-PARSE-LICENSE.txt`, `ZSTDDEC-LICENSE.txt`, `JSEP-LICENSE`,
  `JSZIP-LICENSE`) — copy the corresponding package's `LICENSE`/`LICENSE.md`
  from `node_modules/` whenever that package's version is bumped.

Recommendation: keep every hand-applied difference from upstream recorded as
a `.patch` file under `patches/` (as done here for `three.core.js`), rather
than only in memory or a commit message. When a pinned version is upgraded,
the workflow is: copy the fresh upstream file in, try to reapply the stored
patch, and only hand-resolve conflicts if the patch fails — instead of trying
to remember from scratch which lines were changed and why.
